description_good_justification: The README's abstract and section 1 say what Deep32 does (it answers network and security engineering questions from a local corpus of RFCs and Cisco documentation through MCP tools for Claude Code and Codex) and which problem it addresses: four common kinds of error in model answers about network protocols. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32#readme, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/README.md#abstract.
interact_justification: The README gives the install commands and a "Contributing and support" section that points to Discussions, Issues, SECURITY.md and CONTRIBUTING.md. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/README.md#contributing-and-support.
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the process: an issue first for larger changes, pull requests against main, and what a change must include. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/CONTRIBUTING.md.
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md section 4.2 lists the requirements: tests for new behavior, passing suites, no new lint findings, each file's existing style, American spelling, and documentation for anything a user can see. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/CONTRIBUTING.md#42-what-a-change-includes.
floss_license_justification: The code is licensed under the Apache License 2.0; the parts that use MuPDF (the Forge's PDF converter and the Workstation Library's renderer e26-render) are AGPL-3.0-or-later; the documentation is CC BY 4.0. Third-party models and documents keep their own terms and are not part of the software. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/LICENSE, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/NOTICE, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/licenses/LICENSING.md.
floss_license_osi_justification: Apache-2.0 and AGPL-3.0-or-later are both OSI-approved. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/LICENSE.
license_location_justification: LICENSE is at the repository root, with LICENSE-DOCS and the licenses folder beside it. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/LICENSE.
documentation_basics_justification: The README describes the system and its install, INSTALL.md has every procedure with its verification, docs/HARDWARE.md covers sizing, and the design document D32-TR-1 specifies each part. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/INSTALL.md, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/tr/README.md.
documentation_interface_justification: README section 6 lists the eleven MCP tools and what each returns; the interface contracts C1 to C10 specify the formats and protocols between the parts. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/README.md#6-tools-and-answer-protocol, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/contracts/README.md.
sites_https_justification: The repository, releases and Discussions are on github.com, the images on archive.org and the DOI on doi.org, all served over HTTPS. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32, https://archive.org/details/deep32-0.1.0-alpha.2.
discussion_justification: GitHub Discussions: searchable, every thread has its own URL, and anyone can join with a free account in a web browser. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/discussions.
english_justification: All documentation is in English, and bug reports, pull requests and questions are accepted in English; CONTRIBUTING.md section 1 asks for English in Discussions. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/CONTRIBUTING.md#1-questions.
maintained_justification: Releases 0.1.0-alpha.1 and 0.1.0-alpha.2 in November 2026. No issues have been filed yet, and SECURITY.md commits to acknowledging a security report within 7 days. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/CHANGELOG.md, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/SECURITY.md.
repo_public_justification: The source is in a public Git repository on GitHub. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32.
repo_track_justification: Git records what changed, who changed it and when, and commits and tags are signed. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/commits/main.
repo_interim_justification: The public repository holds interim versions between releases: after the v0.1.0-alpha.1 tag it has more than a dozen commits with code and documentation changes. Work that contains lab details or private names is published once it has been scrubbed. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/compare/v0.1.0-alpha.1...main.
version_unique_justification: Each release has its own version number (0.1.0-alpha.1, 0.1.0-alpha.2). Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/CHANGELOG.md.
version_semver_justification: Versions follow Semantic Versioning, as the release notes state. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/CHANGELOG.md.
version_tags_justification: Each release has a signed Git tag (v0.1.0-alpha.1, v0.1.0-alpha.2). Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/tags.
release_notes_justification: CHANGELOG.md has hand-written notes for each release, with what was added, changed and fixed and the known issues. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/CHANGELOG.md.
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerability has been fixed in any release so far. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/CHANGELOG.md.
report_process_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md section 2 and the bug report form say how to report a bug and what to include. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/CONTRIBUTING.md#2-bug-reports, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/issues/new/choose.
report_responses_justification: No bug reports have been filed since the repository opened on 14 November 2026; reports are acknowledged as they arrive. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/issues?q=is%3Aissue.
enhancement_responses_justification: No enhancement requests have been filed yet. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/issues?q=is%3Aissue.
report_archive_justification: GitHub Issues and Discussions are public and searchable. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/issues, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/discussions.
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md describes how to report a vulnerability, and the README links to it. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/SECURITY.md.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled, and SECURITY.md also gives an email address and the OpenPGP key to encrypt to. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/SECURITY.md#2-reporting-a-vulnerability, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/security/advisories/new.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports have been received in the last 6 months. SECURITY.md commits to acknowledging a report within 7 days. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/SECURITY.md.
build_justification: The Python and shell programs run from source with no build step. The release images are built from hash-verified inputs by the build scripts in src/build and src/gpu-pack/build on dedicated build hosts, and the Library (C99) builds with GNU make on OpenBSD. docs/BUILDING.md describes both. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/BUILDING.md#4-building-the-images, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/src/build/README.md, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/src/gpu-pack/PACK.md.
build_common_tools_justification: GNU make, Docker, Python and a POSIX shell. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/BUILDING.md#4-building-the-images.
build_floss_tools_justification: Every build tool is FLOSS: OpenBSD and its compiler, GNU make, Docker Engine, Python and bash. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/BUILDING.md#4-building-the-images.
test_justification: FLOSS automated test suites, most written with Python's unittest and the rest as small Python or PowerShell test runners; python -I -B tests/run_all.py runs them all, and docs/BUILDING.md section 2 documents the runner and each suite. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/BUILDING.md#2-running-the-tests.
test_invocation_justification: make check (or make test) runs every suite through python -I -B tests/run_all.py, which runs each suite the way it expects to be run (most are standard unittest files; the rest are small Python runners and one PowerShell script), skips with a reason what the machine can't run, and exits non-zero on any failure. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/Makefile, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/tests/run_all.py, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/BUILDING.md#21-one-command.
test_most_justification: A coverage measurement on 19 November 2026 found 54.0% of the Python statements and 46.0% of its branches covered; the Coverage workflow measures it on each push to main. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ROADMAP.md#51-tests-and-coverage, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/.github/workflows/coverage.yml.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: The Tests workflow runs Ruff and Bandit on Ubuntu and every test suite on Windows for each push and pull request to main. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/.github/workflows/tests.yml, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/actions.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md section 4.2: new behavior comes with tests, and a bug fix comes with a test that fails without the fix. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/CONTRIBUTING.md#42-what-a-change-includes.
tests_are_added_justification: Changes in 0.1.0-alpha.2 added tests with their code, for example tests/release-tools/test_sbom_public_path.py, src/gpu-pack/tests/test_converter_debs.py and tests/relay/test_claude_trace_2_1_326.py. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/tests/release-tools/test_sbom_public_path.py, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/src/gpu-pack/tests/test_converter_debs.py, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/tests/relay/test_claude_trace_2_1_326.py.
tests_documented_added_justification: The pull request template's checklist and CONTRIBUTING.md section 4.2 ask for tests. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md.
warnings_justification: Ruff checks the Python code with a named rule set (ruff.toml) on every push, and the Library builds with -Wall -Wextra -Werror -pedantic. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/ruff.toml, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/src/workstation/library/Makefile.
warnings_fixed_justification: Every warning was reviewed on 19 November 2026 and none is a defect. The remaining Ruff findings outside the image source (41 in 184,075 checked lines) are listed per file in ruff.toml, so any new finding fails CI. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/ruff.toml, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/BUILDING.md#3-lint-and-static-analysis.
warnings_strict_justification: Ruff runs all of its error-class rule families (syntax errors, Pyflakes, Pylint errors, flake8-bugbear) with the reviewed findings listed per file, and every C Makefile builds with -Wall -Wextra -Werror (the Library also with -pedantic). Some builds are not yet maximally strict: the d32log build script and the SQLite build in src/workstation/pyrag/build-py312.sh pass no warning flags, and the Library builds kwaj.c with -Wno-pedantic. All three change the image source; the roadmap plans warnings as errors for every C program in 0.1.0-alpha.3. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/ruff.toml, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ROADMAP.md#3-010-alpha3.
know_secure_design_justification: The design keeps secrets off the images, gives each part its own credentials made at install, pairs parts with SPAKE2 codes that last five minutes, uses TLS between the parts (TLS 1.3 only on the pairing and Ask links) and treats retrieved text as untrusted. The README's security section and the design document go through it threat by threat. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/README.md#10-security-considerations, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/tr/README.md.
know_common_errors_justification: The code compares bearer tokens in constant time, runs subprocesses with argument lists and no shell, and treats retrieved text as untrusted input; Bandit and CodeQL check for common errors on every push. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/README.md#10-security-considerations, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/BUILDING.md#3-lint-and-static-analysis.
crypto_published_justification: Only published algorithms and protocols: SPAKE2 (RFC 9382) on P-256 with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, HMAC-SHA256, SHA-256, TLS 1.3 and OpenPGP signatures with an Ed25519 key. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/contracts/C8-network.md, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ASSURANCE-CASE.md#91-where-it-is-used.
crypto_call_justification: The SPAKE2 exchange and its P-256 arithmetic are implemented in Python inside Deep32 (deep32net/spake2.py and p256.py), because the pairing helper has to run on a host's system Python with only the standard library. The code is checked against the four RFC 9382 Appendix B test vectors, and the header of p256.py says it is not constant-time. All other cryptography calls dedicated libraries: Python's hashlib, hmac, secrets and ssl modules, pyca/cryptography and pyOpenSSL in the Ask relay, LibreSSL's libtls in the Workstation's Ask link, GnuPG and OpenBSD's signify. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/tests/pairing/reference/vectors/pairing-v2-vectors.json.
crypto_floss_justification: Python's standard library on OpenSSL or LibreSSL, GnuPG, and Tailscale's open-source client.
crypto_keylength_justification: P-256 and Ed25519 (128-bit security), SHA-256, and TLS 1.3 only on the pairing and Ask links; nothing smaller is offered. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/adapters/relay/deep32_relay/tls.py.
crypto_working_justification: No broken algorithm is used for security. SHA-1 appears only where an outside format defines it: OpenPGP v4 fingerprints, and git blob IDs when model files are resolved, and those files are also pinned by SHA-256. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/src/release-tools/openpgp_pub.py.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: The default mechanisms avoid algorithms with known serious weaknesses; SHA-1 is used only as the identifiers outside formats define. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/src/release-tools/openpgp_pub.py.
crypto_pfs_justification: The pairing and Ask links use TLS 1.3 only, with ephemeral key agreement, and each SPAKE2 run uses fresh random scalars. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/adapters/relay/deep32_relay/tls.py.
crypto_password_storage_justification: Deep32 stores no user passwords. Machines authenticate with random tokens made at install, and a pairing code is used once and lasts five minutes. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/INSTALL.md#11-what-is-never-stored.
crypto_random_justification: Tokens, nonces and keys come from cryptographically secure generators: Python's secrets module, openssl rand (LibreSSL) for the Workstation's per-install tokens at first boot, arc4random_buf in the Workstation's C code, and the TLS libraries' own generators for key pairs. Python's random module is used only for seeded or trace sampling, never for tokens, nonces or keys. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/src/workstation/distrib/site/usr/local/d32/sbin/d32-firstboot, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ASSURANCE-CASE.md#91-where-it-is-used.
delivery_mitm_justification: Downloads use HTTPS (GitHub, archive.org), and every image is checked against a checksum list signed with the release key. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/README.md#11-release-and-verification.
delivery_unsigned_justification: deep32-get checks the signature on SHA256SUMS and the signer's fingerprint before it uses any hash in the list. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/README.md#11-release-and-verification.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No vulnerability of medium or higher severity in Deep32 has been publicly known for more than 60 days without a fix. OSV-Scanner reports the advisories published for the third-party packages Deep32 pins; I checked each one against how Deep32 uses the package and recorded the result in the OpenVEX document for 0.1.0-alpha.2, which marks all 74 advisories not_affected and gives the reason for each. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/security/README.md, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/security/deep32-0.1.0-alpha.2.openvex.json, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/.github/workflows/osv-scanner.yml.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: Every tracked file was scanned for credentials before the release; each install makes its own tokens and keys, and the tests use labeled synthetic values only. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/INSTALL.md#11-what-is-never-stored.
static_analysis_justification: Ruff and Bandit were run on the release source before the release (19 November 2026), and CodeQL analyzes the Python and C code on every push. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/BUILDING.md#3-lint-and-static-analysis, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/.github/workflows/codeql.yml.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: Bandit's security rules (injection, unsafe deserialization and XML, weak hashes, temporary files, binding) run on every push with a reviewed baseline, CodeQL's security queries analyze the Python and C code, and Flawfinder, which maps its hits to CWE entries, was run over all of the C and C++ on 19 November 2026 with every hit at levels 4 and 5 read by hand. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/bandit.yaml, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/.github/workflows/codeql.yml, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/SECURITY-REVIEW-2026-11.md#5-static-analysis.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: No medium or high finding was confirmed as exploitable; each one was reviewed, and the review is summarized in docs/BUILDING.md section 3. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/BUILDING.md#3-lint-and-static-analysis.
static_analysis_often_justification: CodeQL runs on every push and pull request and weekly, and Ruff and Bandit run on every push and pull request. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/.github/workflows/codeql.yml, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/.github/workflows/tests.yml.
dynamic_analysis_justification: libFuzzer with AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer was applied to the Workstation's C parsers before the release: each of the 17 targets ran for 15 minutes on 19 November 2026 (279 million executions in all), and the Fuzz workflow runs every target on each push and pull request to main and for 30 minutes weekly. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/tests/fuzz/README.md#6-results, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/.github/workflows/fuzz.yml.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The C code is fuzzed with libFuzzer together with AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: 17 targets cover the vector kernel, the Library's JSON, base64, text, image, document and media readers and its decompressor, the Ask link's framing and message parsing, and the address parser. The Fuzz workflow runs them on every push and pull request to main and weekly. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/tests/fuzz/README.md, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/.github/workflows/fuzz.yml.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The fuzz targets are built without NDEBUG, so the assertions in the C code stay on; each harness checks its own invariants with FUZZ_ASSERT (round trips, bounds, agreement between two implementations), and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer stops at the first problem (-fno-sanitize-recover=all). Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/tests/fuzz/README.md#1-what-is-fuzzed, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/tests/fuzz/fuzz.h.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: The fuzzing on 19 November 2026 found five defects, all rated low and none exploitable at medium or higher severity; their fixes ship with the next release that rebuilds the images, 0.1.0-alpha.3. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/tests/fuzz/README.md#5-findings.
dco_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md section 5 asks every contributor to sign off each commit with git commit -s, which certifies the Developer Certificate of Origin 1.1; the pull request template has the same item. Section 5 of the Apache License 2.0 covers the license of code contributions. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/CONTRIBUTING.md#5-licensing-of-contributions, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md.
governance_justification: GOVERNANCE.md describes the lead-maintainer model: anyone can propose a change in an issue or a pull request, and the project lead decides. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/GOVERNANCE.md.
code_of_conduct_justification: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, adapted from the Contributor Covenant 2.1, says what is expected and how to report a problem, and CONTRIBUTING.md section 6 points to it. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/CONTRIBUTING.md#6-conduct.
roles_responsibilities_justification: GOVERNANCE.md lists the roles (project lead, co-maintainer, contributor), who holds each one, and their rights and duties. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/GOVERNANCE.md#roles.
access_continuity_justification: GOVERNANCE.md, section Continuity, describes the continuity plan: a GitHub account successor who can take over the repository, and a sealed backup of the release signing key that is released to that person only if the lead is confirmed unable to continue. Both are in place. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/GOVERNANCE.md.
bus_factor_justification: Single maintainer; continuity arranged through the GitHub account successor and a sealed signing-key backup (GOVERNANCE.md). Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity.
documentation_roadmap_justification: docs/ROADMAP.md says what I intend through November 2027, release by release and including the OpenSSF practice work, and section 7 says what Deep32 will not do, each item tied to a recorded design decision. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ROADMAP.md, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ROADMAP.md#7-what-deep32-will-not-do.
documentation_architecture_justification: README section 4 describes the architecture, the design document D32-TR-1 specifies each part and how they connect, and the interface contracts C1 to C10 specify the formats and protocols between the parts. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/README.md#4-architecture, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/tr/README.md, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/contracts/README.md.
documentation_security_justification: README section 10 describes the security design, SECURITY.md sections 5 and 7 say what users can and cannot expect, docs/ASSURANCE-CASE.md states the security requirements and argues them, and INSTALL.md section 11 lists every credential and where it is made. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/README.md#10-security-considerations, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/SECURITY.md#7-what-you-can-and-cannot-expect, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ASSURANCE-CASE.md#2-security-requirements, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/INSTALL.md#11-what-is-never-stored.
documentation_quick_start_justification: The README's Quick start gives the two commands that clone the repository and run the setup script on each machine; the script checks the machine, downloads and verifies the images and installs. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/README.md#quick-start.
documentation_current_justification: The README and the user and project pages (INSTALL.md, SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, the agent adapters page, and the pages in docs/ on hardware, optional features, decisions, upgrading, building, the roadmap, the assurance case, the security review and known vulnerabilities) say which release they apply to, and CONTRIBUTING.md section 4.2 requires a change to update the page that describes the behavior. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/CONTRIBUTING.md#42-what-a-change-includes.
documentation_achievements_justification: The README's badge row links to the project's OpenSSF Best Practices page, and the badge shows the level reached. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/README.md.
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: Every image in the documentation has alt text, and every drawn figure has a light and a dark version; the screenshots have one version. The project's sites are GitHub and the Internet Archive. The Workstation's desktop programs have not been checked with a screen reader or for keyboard-only use. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/README.md.
internationalization_justification: The interface and the documentation are in English only, and so is the corpus; translations are not planned for the next year. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ROADMAP.md#7-what-deep32-will-not-do.
sites_password_security_justification: The project's sites are GitHub, the Internet Archive and Zenodo; the project runs no site of its own and stores no passwords.
maintenance_or_update_justification: docs/UPGRADING.md gives the upgrade path for each part of an install: what it keeps, what it makes again and the order of the steps. SECURITY.md section 1 says which releases get fixes. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/UPGRADING.md, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/SECURITY.md#1-supported-releases.
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No vulnerability report has been resolved in the last 12 months. SECURITY.md commits to naming the reporter in the advisory and the release notes. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/SECURITY.md#6-what-happens-after-a-report.
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: SECURITY.md section 6 documents what happens after a report: acknowledgement within 7 days, triage and a severity on GitHub's scale, a private fix with a test in a security advisory, the release, disclosure with a CVE, and credit. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/SECURITY.md#6-what-happens-after-a-report.
coding_standards_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md asks contributors to keep each file's existing style and American spelling, and ruff.toml names the Python rule set, but no coding standard is named yet for each language. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/CONTRIBUTING.md#42-what-a-change-includes, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ROADMAP.md#53-static-analysis-coding-standards-and-dependencies.
coding_standards_enforced_justification: Ruff enforces its error-class rules on the Python code on every push, but no style standard is enforced yet for Python, C, shell or PowerShell. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/ruff.toml, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ROADMAP.md#53-static-analysis-coding-standards-and-dependencies.
build_standard_variables_justification: Most C builds pass CC, CFLAGS and LDFLAGS, but the Library's makefile doesn't pass LDFLAGS to its link lines or honor CXXFLAGS, and several build scripts call cc with fixed flags, for example src/workstation/node/build.sh and src/workstation/ship/u2/hardening/build.sh. The fix changes the image source and is listed for 0.1.0-alpha.3. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ROADMAP.md#3-010-alpha3.
build_preserve_debug_justification: Two desktop tools are stripped when they are installed; stripping that can be turned off is listed for 0.1.0-alpha.3. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ROADMAP.md#3-010-alpha3.
build_non_recursive_justification: The desktop programs under src/workstation/ship/u10/src build their shared libraries with recursive make calls; a non-recursive build is listed for 0.1.0-alpha.3. The Library's makefile is non-recursive. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ROADMAP.md#3-010-alpha3.
build_repeatable_justification: Part of the build is shown to be repeatable: the GPU pack's producer builds its shared core twice and stops unless both are byte-identical. A second build of every image, compared byte for byte, hasn't been done yet. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/src/gpu-pack/build/alpha2_disc3.py, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ROADMAP.md#54-builds.
installation_common_justification: The Workstation is a disk image installed by a guided installer, the GPU pack's Docker images are loaded by the Forge's installer, the setup script installs and checks each machine, and INSTALL.md section 10 describes removal. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/INSTALL.md, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/INSTALL.md#10-afterwards.
installation_standard_variables_justific: No installer writes built files into a host's file tree: the Workstation installs from a disk image onto its own disk, the Forge loads container images into Docker and keeps its data in the folder given by its --data-root option, and Connect writes into the agent profile it is given. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/INSTALL.md#5-install-the-forge.
installation_development_quick_justifica: For the Python, shell and PowerShell code a clone, Python 3.12 and make test are enough, and the fuzz targets build with clang on Linux with one command. The Workstation's desktop programs build only on an OpenBSD build host, and there is no public recipe for one yet. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/BUILDING.md#21-one-command, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/tests/fuzz/README.md#2-running-the-targets, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/BUILDING.md#4-building-the-images.
external_dependencies_justification: notices/DEPENDENCIES.tsv lists the third-party components with their version, origin and license note; the Python lock files pin exact versions with hashes; model files and container images are pinned by digest; each release image has an SPDX 2.3 bill of materials. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/notices/DEPENDENCIES.tsv, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/SECURITY.md#8-third-party-components.
dependency_monitoring_justification: OSV-Scanner checks every pinned Python package against the OSV database on each push and pull request and weekly. Findings in the pins the release images are built from go to code scanning; a known vulnerability in any other pin fails the workflow. Each advisory reported in the image pins is triaged and recorded in the release's OpenVEX document, and osv-scanner.toml carries the ones marked not_affected with their reasons. Dependabot updates the GitHub Actions. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/.github/workflows/osv-scanner.yml, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/osv-scanner.toml, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/security/README.md, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/SECURITY.md#8-third-party-components.
updateable_reused_components_justificati: Third-party packages come from package managers and are pinned in lock files, by image digest or by hash, so each one is updated by moving its pin, and d32log compiles Arm's log routine from a pinned optimized-routines release. The vendor folders hold copies of Deep32's own modules, except the Ask link's BIP-39 English word list, which is pinned by its SHA-256 in the SOURCE.txt beside it. The few third-party files copied into the source (that word list, CDE's calculator catalog, palettes and configuration text, and a test-only glibc header) are named with their origin in REUSE.toml and are updated by replacing the copy. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/SECURITY.md#8-third-party-components, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/REUSE.toml.
interfaces_current_justification: The suites run on Python 3.12 to 3.15, the links between the parts use TLS 1.3 (1.2 at the least), and the Workstation runs a current OpenBSD release. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/BUILDING.md#24-results-for-010-alpha2.
automated_integration_testing_justificat: The Tests workflow runs Ruff, Bandit and every suite on each push and pull request to main, the Fuzz workflow fuzzes the C parsers on the same events, and the Coverage workflow measures coverage on each push to main. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/.github/workflows/tests.yml, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/.github/workflows/fuzz.yml, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/actions.
test_statement_coverage80_justification: A measurement on 19 November 2026 found 54.0% of the Python statements covered; the C, shell and PowerShell code isn't measured yet. Raising coverage area by area to 80% is planned. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ROADMAP.md#51-tests-and-coverage, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/.github/workflows/coverage.yml.
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md section 4.2: new behavior comes with tests, and a bug fix comes with a test that fails without the fix, for every change, the maintainer's included. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/CONTRIBUTING.md#42-what-a-change-includes.
implement_secure_design_justification: docs/ASSURANCE-CASE.md section 5 applies each of Saltzer and Schroeder's principles with the code as evidence: a firewall that denies by default, services that refuse to start without a token and refuse requests without a usable one, one user per service with pledge and unveil, containers without capabilities, optional features off by default, and no release metadata parsed before its signature is checked. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ASSURANCE-CASE.md#5-secure-design-principles.
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: TLS negotiates its cipher suite and the release verifier accepts any key named with --key and --fingerprint, but pairing (SPAKE2 on P-256), the Ask link's words and the release signatures (Ed25519) each use one algorithm. A broken one is replaced by a new protocol version, which the pairing HELLO's versions and features fields allow for, or by a new key in a new release. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ASSURANCE-CASE.md#92-criteria.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: Every credential that crosses between machines is its own protected file and is replaced by pairing again, without recompiling. The exception is the engine token, which never leaves the Workstation: it is written into the engine's and the gateway's root-only environment files beside their settings. Giving it a file of its own changes the Workstation image. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ASSURANCE-CASE.md#92-criteria.
crypto_used_network_justification: Traffic between machines is WireGuard (Tailscale), and every Deep32 protocol on top of it is HTTPS or TLS 1.3. Plain HTTP is used only on loopback, on UNIX sockets and on the Forge's internal Docker network inside one host; downloads are checked against signed digests, and the image downloader refuses a redirect from HTTPS to HTTP. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ASSURANCE-CASE.md#92-criteria.
crypto_tls12_justification: Every TLS connection Deep32 configures uses TLS 1.2 or later: pairing and the relay allow only TLS 1.3, the Forge link sets 1.2 as its minimum, and downloads use Python's default context. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ASSURANCE-CASE.md#92-criteria.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: Certificates are verified by default: the getter, Connect and the Forge link use CA verification, and the Ask link and the relay check the peer against its pinned SHA-256. Pairing turns CA checks off on purpose, because no CA can know the new certificates: both certificate pins are mixed into the SPAKE2 password scalar, so a certificate that doesn't match fails key confirmation. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ASSURANCE-CASE.md#92-criteria.
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: A token is sent only after the peer is verified: the Forge token only on a connection whose certificate and host name were checked, Connect's only over verified HTTPS with redirects refused, and in pairing only after the joiner's key confirmation verifies. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ASSURANCE-CASE.md#92-criteria.
signed_releases_justification: Each release's checksum list (SHA256SUMS) has a detached OpenPGP signature by the release key, whose fingerprint is in the README and SECURITY.md; deep32-get checks the signature and the signer's fingerprint before it uses any hash in the list. The Workstation image is also signed with signify. The private key isn't stored on GitHub or the download site. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/README.md#11-release-and-verification, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/SECURITY.md#2-reporting-a-vulnerability.
version_tags_signed_justification: Release tags are signed (v0.1.0-alpha.1, v0.1.0-alpha.2), and docs/UPGRADING.md shows how to check one with git verify-tag. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/tags, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/UPGRADING.md#1-before-you-start.
input_validation_justification: Every input from an untrusted source is checked against an allowlist: MCP tool arguments are typed and bounded, Host and Origin are allowlisted with a body limit, pairing messages are strict JSON with exact key sets and bounded certificates, Ask link frames have size and type limits, and release metadata and the content manifest are checked against schemas and safe paths and URLs after their signatures. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ASSURANCE-CASE.md#7-input-validation.
hardening_justification: The Workstation runs OpenBSD with W^X, position-independent executables and system libraries relinked in random order at boot, at securelevel 1 with system files immutable and a hardened sysctl set; most C programs build with -fstack-protector-strong. The Forge's containers drop all capabilities, run with no-new-privileges, have read-only root file systems where possible, and the PDF converter has no network. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ASSURANCE-CASE.md#8-hardening.
assurance_case_justification: docs/ASSURANCE-CASE.md states the security requirements, the threat model and its entry points, the trust boundaries, how secure design principles are applied, and how each of the 2025 CWE Top 25 is countered or doesn't apply, with the code as evidence for each claim and the residual risks listed. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ASSURANCE-CASE.md.
copyright_per_file_justification: REUSE.toml records the copyright holder of every file in the REUSE format. The Library renderer e26-render, some of the PDF converter's files and the fuzz targets carry their own copyright line, but most source files don't carry one yet. Adding them to the image source changes the images and is planned for 0.1.0-alpha.3. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/REUSE.toml, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ROADMAP.md#55-license-metadata.
license_per_file_justification: REUSE.toml records the license of every file. The Library renderer e26-render, some of the PDF converter's files and the fuzz targets carry an SPDX-License-Identifier line, but most source files don't carry one yet. Adding them to the image source is planned for 0.1.0-alpha.3. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/REUSE.toml, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ROADMAP.md#55-license-metadata.
small_tasks_justification: No issues are labeled for newcomers yet; I'll open small issues labeled good first issue when I invite contributors. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ROADMAP.md#57-people.
require_2FA_justification: SECURITY.md section 9: anyone who can change the repository or read its private vulnerability reports must use two-factor authentication on their GitHub account, and write access is given only to an account that does. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/SECURITY.md#9-maintainer-accounts.
secure_2FA_justification: SECURITY.md section 9 requires a passkey, a security key or an authenticator app; a text-message code alone doesn't meet it. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/SECURITY.md#9-maintainer-accounts.
code_review_standards_justification: GOVERNANCE.md says how review works and what it checks: that the change is worthwhile, that the tests and checks pass, and that it brings in no known security problem; CONTRIBUTING.md section 4.2 says what a change must include. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/GOVERNANCE.md#reviews, https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/CONTRIBUTING.md#42-what-a-change-includes.
build_reproducible_justification: The images are built from hash-checked inputs on dedicated build hosts, but there is no public rebuild guide yet and no independent rebuild has been compared with a release. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ROADMAP.md#54-builds.
test_statement_coverage90_justification: 54.0% of the Python statements were covered on 19 November 2026; the plan is in the roadmap. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ROADMAP.md#51-tests-and-coverage.
test_branch_coverage80_justification: 46.0% of the Python branches were covered on 19 November 2026; the plan is in the roadmap. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ROADMAP.md#51-tests-and-coverage.
hardened_site_justification: The repository and releases are on GitHub, which sends the hardening headers. The images download from the Internet Archive, whose pages don't send all of them, and the project can't change that; a download mirror under my control is under consideration. Evidence: https://github.com/hellobpdu/deep32/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/docs/ROADMAP.md#6-under-consideration.
